title: Sliding Window Maximum
summary: Report the largest value in every window of fixed width as it slides.
statement:
A window of width `k` slides across `nums` one position at a time. Return the maximum inside the window at every position, left to right.

### Constraints

- 1 ≤ nums.length ≤ 100,000
- 1 ≤ k ≤ nums.length
- -10⁹ ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10⁹

### Example

```
nums = [1, 3, -1, -3, 5, 3, 6, 7], k = 3
```

gives `[3, 3, 5, 5, 6, 7]` — one value per window position.

> **Rescanning each window is too slow**
>
> That is O(n·k), and the largest hidden case makes it hurt. Keep a deque of indices whose values are decreasing: before pushing a new index, drop every index at the back whose value is smaller, since none of them can ever be the maximum again while the new one is in the window. The front is then always the current maximum, and each index enters and leaves once.

visibleTests.explanation: A decreasing array: each window's first value wins.
